note: Every claim SPEC.md flagged as risky, checked against source (kode-digital/bos-mirror) on 2026-08-28. All are status needs_review per SPEC.md instruction — code review alone cannot authorize a marketing claim, but it can tell us whether the underlying feature exists at all. Do not write narration against any claim here until it moves to status verified by the product owner.

claims.evidence: Modules/Attendance and app/Http/Controllers/ClockInClockOutController.php contain no geofencing, GPS/lat-long capture, or photo/selfie verification of any kind — grepped attendance migrations and controllers, found none. Attendance appears to be a plain timestamp clock-in/out with no location or identity verification at all.
claims.recommendation: This claim is more overstated than SPEC.md's original worry (which assumed geofencing existed but could be spoofed). As written it should not be used. Rewrite around what's true — e.g. 'clock-in/out tracked automatically' — unless the product owner confirms a verification mechanism exists that this review missed.

claims.status: needs_review — new evidence narrows this significantly
claims.severity: medium — no documented basis found, and the candidate feature is narrower than assumed
claims.evidence: No benchmark, timing log, or documented baseline found in code. The BOQ document-scan OCR flow (Modules/CRM/App/Services/SiteVisitDocumentOcrService.php, Google Vision-based) was the assumed candidate, but live capture testing (2026-09-03) found it is not a generic 'scan any site document' feature: BoqScanController@store defaults to a single hard-coded extraction template, CrmDocumentTemplate code='MAMMO_PREINSTALL_BOQ' (Modules/CRM/database/seeders/MammoPreInstallationBoqTemplateSeeder.php), and it is the only template seeded anywhere in the codebase. That template's layout_definition is a fixed normalised-coordinate column map (item/description/unit/quantity/rate/amount bands, expected_aspect_ratio 0.7071) built from one specific real pre-printed physical form used for mammography equipment pre-installation work — a different customer vertical (medical equipment installers) from Kunos's stated positioning (hardware stores, retail, warehousing). A generic warehouse/hardware-style document uploaded against this template extracted 0 rows in a real test run.
claims.recommendation: Do not use the 80% figure, and do not narrate the BOQ scan feature as general-purpose document-to-quote OCR for a hardware-store audience — as implemented today it only works for the one Mammo pre-installation form layout. Either: (a) the product owner confirms other templates exist that this review didn't see (e.g. added via an admin UI rather than a seeder) and points to one relevant to hardware/warehousing, or (b) V1's boq_scan_to_quote shot needs to use the real Mammo-form scenario and narrate it honestly (a different customer story than 'Aurora Hardware'), or (c) the shot target changes again to something that fits the hardware/warehouse positioning without this template lock-in.

claims.claim: literally three seconds for the Kunos AI quote
claims.status: skipped — scene dropped from V1, not filming this claim
claims.severity: critical — this was SPEC.md's original V1 target shot
claims.evidence: The Kunos AI chat assistant (App\Http\Controllers\BosAiAssistantController, Anthropic-backed) supports exactly three actions — prepare_leave_application, prepare_domestic_travel_claim, search_leave_on_behalf_staff — all HR. It has no client lookup, stock check, or quote-generation capability. CRM quotations (Modules/CRM/App/Http/Controllers/QuotationController.php) exist and work, but as a conventional multi-step manual form with zero AI or chat involvement.
claims.recommendation: Decision made 2026-08-28: skip this scene rather than wait on product-owner confirmation. V1 target shot changed to boq_scan_to_quote (real, working OCR-driven flow) — see SPEC.md Status section. This claim/shot can be revisited later as a separate video if the AI-chat-quote feature is ever built, but it is off the table for V1.

claims.claim: fastest delivery route powered by Google Maps live traffic
claims.severity: critical — feature does not appear to exist at all
claims.evidence: Transport module's only controller (Modules/Transport/app/Http/Controllers/KenderaanController.php) implements an internal vehicle-request/approval workflow (staff requests a vehicle, admin/supervisor approves, driver assigned) — not delivery-route planning. Repo-wide search for Google Maps Directions/Distance Matrix API, traffic-model params, or any routing-optimization logic returned nothing.
claims.recommendation: This claim has no code basis whatsoever, not even a partial/unoptimized version. Do not use until the product owner either points to where this actually lives or confirms it needs to be built first.

claims.claim: named accounting integrations (SQL Account, AutoCount) and their availability status
claims.evidence: Repo-wide case-insensitive search for 'SQL Account', 'AutoCount', and common alternatives (Xero, QuickBooks) returned zero matches in code, config, or dependencies. The only related feature is Modules/Finance/App/Http/Controllers/CashbookIntegrationController.php, which is a generic CSV/bank-statement import → classify → approve workflow, not a named accounting-software sync.
claims.recommendation: Do not name SQL Account or AutoCount specifically unless the product owner confirms an integration exists outside this repo (e.g. a separate service) or is genuinely planned. If the real feature is the generic cashbook import, describe it as that instead.

summary_for_product_owner: Of the five flagged claims, two (attendance accuracy, delivery routing) point to features with no code presence at all. One (AI quote) is the V1 target and has no code presence for the specific quoting behavior described, though a related but different AI feature (HR leave assistant) and a related but different fast-processing feature (BOQ OCR scan) do exist and work today. Two (processing time %, named accounting integrations) need either a benchmark or a correction to what's actually integrated.
